sources_considered.why: Contemporaneous primary evaluation of a T5-based system generating and checking factual inference chains.
Verified that the paper was public on October 21, 2022, before the post.
Documents factual reference standards and substantial truthfulness limitations of contemporary models.
Verified the May 8, 2022 version and its availability before the post.
Duplicate publication record for TruthfulQA; the versioned paper provides fuller methods and precise availability.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton and Owain Evans
evidence_items.explanation: The evaluation explicitly uses sourced reference answers, supporting the operational reading of the first clause. Its best tested model produced only 58% true answers, also documenting serious reliability limitations without demonstrating an absence of reasoning.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Allen Institute for AI researchers
evidence_items.locator: Section 5.2, Results; supporting methods and human evaluation in Sections 4.2 and 5.3
evidence_items.explanation: Entailer used a trained T5-11B model to generate and check inference chains, achieving 75.2% and 75.4% accuracy on two question-answering datasets. Human evaluation of explanations for correct answers found that over 70% clearly followed from their premises, contradicting categorical absence under the stated operational reading.

unresolved_gaps: These evaluations do not settle a philosophical claim about understanding or grounding truth.
Entailer does not establish reliable detection of unrestricted social-media misinformation.
Its human explanation evaluation selected correct answers; it is not an unconditional reasoning-success rate.
